texts.label: Cipher telegrams Bogotá <-> Puerto Asís, 9-27 Sept 1932 (GARV..2.2.4, alphabetic system)
texts.summary: Cipher telegrams between the Ministry of War in Bogotá and Gen. Amadeo Rodríguez Vergara, civil and military chief of the Amazonas, at Puerto Asís, 9-27 September 1932, the first weeks after the Peruvian seizure of Leticia (1 Sept 1932): ammunition from Bofors, the gunboats Cartagena, Santa Marta and Barranquilla, the state of the troops (499 men, corrected to 599), the move to Caucayá, the passage of Güepí, the Napo and the risk of a conflict with Ecuador, Peruvian reinforcements to Loreto, censorship of soldiers' letters.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 4 Nov 2026 against translation.md: coherent military Spanish throughout in telegraphic style (troop states, gunboats, Bofors ammunition, the Manaos report on the steamer Nariño, Güepí, the Ecuador/Napo question); keying slips normalised in the reading. Unresolved: zeffe (f. 107), pascama (f. 153), hsla (f. 159), gixhtlo (f. 170); f. 153 does not fully construe around relator/yo. Grade B because the clear words of most telegrams were not transcribed, so the sentences are the cipher parts only.

prior.where: Key in the same fonds (GARV..1.1.4); contemporary clear texts of five telegrams in the file; Daniel Bourdeau's sample reading of ff. 149 and 153 (research/latam_vetting, 28 Oct 2026).

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
